transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Uh, thanks. I guess what brought me in is… I’ve been having a harder time than I’d like to admit staying locked in on things at work. Like I can start a safety briefing or a plan review really trying to pay attention, and then a few minutes later my mind’s already jumped to three other job problems. Then I realize I missed something I really should’ve caught.

I mean, I try to manage it, and I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but it’s been happening enough that I figured I should talk to someone about it.
Is this difficulty with focusing happening only at work or are you also experiencing it in other areas of your life?

No, it’s not just work. Work is where it shows up the most, probably because there are more people depending on me, but… it’s at home too.

I don’t want to make it sound like I’m just careless or something, but I’ve missed follow-ups and had some site coordination stuff get messy enough that my employer actually raised a formal concern. That was pretty embarrassing.

And at home, my wife’s been… patient, but she’s worn out. She has to remind me about things I already said I’d take care of, and I can tell it’s getting old for her. So yeah, it’s more than just work, I guess.
Do you often find yourself fidgeting or feeling restless when you're sitting still?

I’m not totally sure how much is “often,” honestly. I mean, I don’t think of myself as bouncing off the walls or anything like that. But sitting still for a long time… yeah, I can get kind of uncomfortable, I guess.

Like I might shift around, tap my foot, mess with a pen. I don’t always notice it unless someone points it out, or I catch myself doing it. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you often interrupt others or blurt out answers before they've finished speaking?

Yeah… I mean, I try not to, because I know it’s rude. But yes, I do that sometimes.

Like someone will start asking me something, and I think I already know where they’re going with it, so I jump in with the answer before they’re done. Then every now and then I realize I missed the important part they hadn’t even gotten to yet. It’s embarrassing when that happens. I’m not trying to steamroll anybody, I just… answer too fast, I guess.
Do you often act on impulse without thinking things through?

I guess… yes, in the sense that I answer too fast sometimes. I don’t mean to be impulsive, exactly, but if someone starts asking me something, I’ll think I know where they’re going and jump in before they’ve finished.

Then sometimes I realize there was an important part I didn’t let them get to, and I feel pretty dumb about it. I’m trying to be better about waiting, but it still happens. Is that what you mean by acting on impulse?
Have your difficulties with focus, impulsivity, and restlessness caused you significant distress or problems in your relationships or daily life?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t want to make it sound like I’m falling apart or blaming everything on this, but it has caused problems.

At work it’s gotten to where missed follow-ups and me not keeping site coordination organized enough have become a real issue. My employer has brought it up formally, which was… honestly pretty embarrassing.

And at home, my wife gets worn down because I’ll say I’m going to handle something and then she ends up having to remind me again and again. I know that’s frustrating for her. I’m trying, but yes, it’s definitely causing stress.
Have you always had difficulties with focus and impulsivity, or did they start more recently?

I think it’s been there a long time, honestly. I don’t think it just started recently.

I mean, I don’t want to make it sound like I was some terrible kid or anything, but back in elementary school teachers were already telling my parents I couldn’t stay in my seat, I talked out of turn, lost homework… stuff like that. And I’d rush through directions before I really understood what I was supposed to do.

So… yeah, I guess it goes pretty far back. Does that answer what you’re asking?
Do you often feel restless or have trouble engaging in leisure activities quietly?

I’m not totally sure how to answer that. I mean, I don’t think of myself as… unable to relax, exactly.

I do tend to get up and move around if I’m sitting too long, and quiet downtime can feel a little uncomfortable sometimes, but I’ve also kind of gotten used to that being how I am. If we’re watching something, I might be shifting around or needing to do something with my hands.

I don’t know if that counts as “trouble engaging quietly,” though. Does that sound like what you mean?
Do you often feel the need to be active and have trouble sitting still in your daily activities?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I try not to be disruptive about it, but sitting still for long stretches is hard.

Like in meetings, when everyone else can just sit through the whole thing, I’m usually the one standing up, going to get coffee, stepping outside to “check something,” or finding some reason to move around. I tell myself it’s work-related, and sometimes it is, but honestly part of it is just needing to get up.

Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Were you often forgetful or did you often lose things as a child?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t know how bad it was compared to other kids, but I did lose things a lot.

And honestly, it’s kind of still like that now. I’m always patting my pockets or digging through my truck looking for my keys, my tape, notebook, marked-up drawings… sometimes even my phone when I just had it in my hand a minute ago. It’s embarrassing, so I try to make it look like I’m just checking something, but… yeah, that’s pretty common for me. Is that the kind of forgetful you mean?
Have you experienced difficulties with focus, impulsivity, and restlessness consistently throughout your life, including as a child, teenager, and adult?

Yeah… I think it probably has been there the whole time, even if I didn’t really think of it that way.

Back in elementary school, teachers were already telling my parents I couldn’t stay in my seat, talked out of turn, lost homework, and would rush through directions before I really understood what I was supposed to do. I don’t love saying it like that because it sounds like I was just being difficult, but… that was the kind of feedback they got.

So, yeah, I guess it wasn’t just something that showed up as an adult. Does that answer what you’re asking?
Have your difficulties with focus, impulsivity, and restlessness caused problems in your friendships or other social relationships outside of work and home?

I’m not really sure, honestly. I mean… I have friends, and I don’t think people would say I’m impossible to be around or anything like that.

Maybe there have been times where I talk too much or get restless and want to leave early, but I don’t know if I’d call it a major problem. I guess I don’t always notice unless someone points it out. What kind of problems do you mean—like arguments, or people getting frustrated with me?
Have you experienced these difficulties with focus, impulsivity, and restlessness in all the different jobs or roles you've had?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I’ve managed to work and keep moving forward, so I don’t want to make it sound like I can’t do my job.

But if I’m being honest, it’s followed me around. At work lately it’s gotten more noticeable—missed follow-ups, stuff not being coordinated as cleanly on site as it should be. It’s been enough that my employer has raised formal concerns, which is… not great to admit.

And at home, my wife gets worn out having to remind me about things I told her I’d take care of. I know that’s not exactly a job role, but it’s the same pattern, if that makes sense.
Have you lost any friendships because of your difficulties with focus, impulsivity, or restlessness?

I don’t think I’ve outright lost friendships because of it… at least not that anyone has said to me directly.

There are probably people I’ve drifted away from, but I don’t know if that’s because of me being distracted or restless or just life getting busy. I wouldn’t want to blame it on that unless I knew. I guess I’m not totally sure how to answer that.
Have you experienced these difficulties with focus, impulsivity, and restlessness in all areas of your life, including hobbies and other activities outside of work and home?

I’m not totally sure. I mean, outside of work and home… I guess with hobbies or things I try to do, I can be a little inconsistent, but I don’t know if I’d call it a problem exactly.

Like, I’ll start something and then not always keep up with it, or I get restless if it’s not holding my attention. But I don’t know if that’s what you mean. I don’t want to overstate it. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking about?
Have you experienced these difficulties with focus, impulsivity, and restlessness at the same level of severity throughout your childhood, teenage years, and adulthood?

I don’t know if I’d say it was the exact same severity the whole time… but it definitely goes way back.

Like, even in elementary school, teachers were already telling my parents things like I couldn’t stay in my seat, I’d talk out of turn, lose homework, or rush through directions before I really understood what I was supposed to do.

I guess I always hoped I’d just kind of grow out of that, but… yeah, it was there pretty early. Is that the kind of history you mean?
Have you ever had a close friend or family member, outside of your wife, comment on or express concern about your behavior or habits?

Not really, no… at least not that I can think of clearly.

I mean, family might joke about me being kind of scattered or always doing something, but I don’t remember anyone sitting me down and saying they were concerned, if that’s what you mean. Maybe I’m missing something, but outside of my wife, I can’t think of a specific person who’s brought it up seriously.
Have you ever been unable to perform a task or achieve a goal due to your difficulties with focus, impulsivity, or restlessness?

Yeah… I think so. I don’t like saying it that way, because I do try hard, but at work it’s gotten me into trouble.

There have been times where I missed follow-ups or didn’t keep the site coordination organized the way I should have, and it got serious enough that my employer brought it up formally. That was pretty embarrassing.

And at home, my wife gets worn down because I’ll say I’m going to handle something and then she has to remind me again and again. I know that’s not fair to her. So… yes, I guess it has kept me from doing things the way I’m supposed to. Does that answer what you mean?
Have you experienced difficulties with focus, impulsivity, and restlessness in multiple settings, such as school, work, home, and social situations, consistently over the years?

Yeah… I think it’s been in more than one place. I mean, I don’t want to overstate it, but it’s not just something my wife notices at home.

At work, it’s gotten serious enough that missed follow-ups and me not keeping site coordination organized properly led to my employer raising formal concerns. That was hard to hear.

And at home, my wife gets pretty worn down because I’ll say I’m going to take care of something, and then she ends up having to remind me over and over. So… yeah, I guess it has shown up in different settings over the years. Is that what you mean?
Have you ever felt like your difficulties with focus, impulsivity, or restlessness have significantly strained or damaged a relationship with someone other than your wife?

Other than my wife… I’m not sure I can point to a relationship that was really damaged, exactly.

I mean, at work it’s definitely strained things. Missing follow-ups and not keeping the site coordination as organized as I should have got serious enough that my employer formally brought it up, so… I guess that affected trust there. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but it was a real issue.

At home, it’s more my wife who gets worn down having to remind me about things I said I’d handle. So outside of her, I’d say work relationships have been strained more than personal ones. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking?

doctor.question: Have you ever felt like your difficulties with focus, impulsivity, or restlessness have significantly strained or damaged a relationship with someone other than your wife?

target_item.name: Functional Impairment
target_item.manifestation: At work it has gotten bad enough that missed follow-ups and poorly organized site coordination led to formal concern from my employer, and at home my wife is worn down from having to remind me about things I said I would handle.
target_item.reason: The question is asking about significant impairment or damage caused by the symptoms in relationships or functioning, especially beyond home; this profile covers work-related consequences, including formal concern from the employer.

patient.answer:
Other than my wife… I’m not sure I can point to a relationship that was really damaged, exactly.

I mean, at work it’s definitely strained things. Missing follow-ups and not keeping the site coordination as organized as I should have got serious enough that my employer formally brought it up, so… I guess that affected trust there. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but it was a real issue.

At home, it’s more my wife who gets worn down having to remind me about things I said I’d handle. So outside of her, I’d say work relationships have been strained more than personal ones. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking?

opening_question.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient's symptoms of inattention, impulsivity, and restlessness have been present since childhood and have caused significant distress and problems in multiple areas of life, including work, home, and social relationships.
